Stage 1 component distributions. The layer1 layer. Facets show components 1-2 in decomposition
order; stored densities summarize sample-coordinate distributions; rugs mark sample
coordinates; dotted vertical lines mark zero; Density fills, outlines, and rug colours;
baseline stems use line type and height and redundantly encode categorical planted_group. The
analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross_sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive distribution of sample coordinates. No component-selection
threshold is applied. This descriptive gallery does not rank or nominate a biological
coordinate.

Stage 1 decomposition coordinates. Molecular layers layer1, layer2. Facets identify molecular
layers; points show component 1 sample coordinates rank-ordered within each layer; the dotted
horizontal line marks zero; Point colours and point shapes encode categorical planted_group;
The subtitle reports the stored synthetic ground-truth angle for component 1. The analysis unit
is independent biological observation; the design is cross_sectional; the estimand is the
descriptive sample coordinate on component 1. No component-selection threshold is applied. This
display does not select a component or establish biological interpretation.

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. Molecular layers layer1, layer2. The black curve
shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component 1; Rug colours
and baseline stem line type and height redundantly encode categorical planted_group;
Critical-point symbols and barrier-height segments are omitted. The analysis unit is
independent biological observation; the design is cross_sectional; the estimand is the
density-derived quasi-potential along the selected component. No calibrated critical-point or
barrier threshold is applied. The landscape is an exploratory description and does not by
itself establish a biological state transition.

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. Molecular layers layer1, layer2. The black curve
shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component 1; Rug colours
and baseline stem width and height redundantly encode categorical planted_group; Exploratory
downward triangles mark stored wells; symbols are offset from their stored coordinates and
linked by dashed stems; exploratory upward triangles mark stored barriers; symbols are offset
from their stored coordinates and linked by dashed stems; Dotted vertical segments show
point-estimate barrier heights. The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the
design is cross_sectional; the estimand is the density-derived quasi-potential along the
selected component. Critical-point classifications and barrier heights are point estimates
without uncertainty. No calibrated critical-point or barrier threshold is applied. The
landscape is an exploratory description and does not by itself establish a biological state
transition.
